title: China's Longest City Wall Isn't Xi'an's — It's Nanjing's | China Travel Expert
description:
Xi'an gets all the city-wall fame, but it isn't China's longest. That title belongs to Nanjing. When the first Ming emperor made Nanjing his capital in the late 1300s, he ringed it with a brick wall that ran roughly 35 km — among the longest city walls ever built — and over 25 km of it still stands today.

Its south gate, Zhonghua Gate (Zhonghua Men), is the largest castle-style gate in China, a layered fortress of arches and courtyards. In many places you can climb up and walk along the top of the wall, right over the modern city.

With "#ChinaTravel" and the "becoming Chinese" trend all over TikTok right now, this is the heritage walk most first-timers never hear about.

★ Expert Tip: start at Zhonghua Gate and walk the wall toward the East Water Gate for the quietest, best-preserved stretch — early morning light is unbeatable.

南京明城墙：明初修筑，绕城约 35 公里，现存超过 25 公里；中华门是中国最大的瓮城式城门。比西安城墙还长。
